rationale: A Sass variable is assigned in SEVERAL places by design — a `!default` at the top and an override inside a theme — so the identity ruling that the CSS lane established, `(kind, resolved name)` with scope kept as provenance, is the load-bearing pin here. `$brand` is assigned twice and must be ONE symbol, or a `references` edge addresses one of two indistinguishable rows. The pins are per-NAME rather than a total, because a total would also pass if the lane published `$brand` once and `$pad` zero times. `!default` and `!global` are recorded as facts on the symbol rather than parsed away: they change what an assignment MEANS — a default is overridable, a global assignment leaks out of its scope — and `$a: 1 !default;` did not parse at all before grammar patch 2/2, at 210 occurrences in the corpus. Every relationship here also pins its LINE, and that is not decoration: the `line-numbers-dropped` mutant removes `line_number` from every edge, which changes no symbol and no edge COUNT, and it SURVIVED until these pins existed. Line provenance is the one class a counting gate cannot see, so it has to be asserted directly (M59/#855).
